Repurposed dead unit 52 of block-0 MLP detects neutral tokens with pT < 1.5e-3 of jet pT and writes a saturating flag; rank-1 key edits in body layers 1-7 and both classifier layers send flagged keys to -15 logits. Expect most of the soft-photon response removed, layer-0 leak remains.

Same detector+corner flag as pass 11 but key-gate strength cut ~4x (target gap -7 for 95% of queries, G capped at 40), which should remove most of the clean-jet damage that came from gate noise on normal keys.
Diagnose pass 12: check where detector unit 52 fires on clean jets; I expect it to fire on ~2.6% of neutral tokens only. If it fires broadly the detector linearisation is wrong.
Ablation: only the rank-1 key gates of pass 12, no detector/flag. If clean damage is still large, the gate noise on normal keys (not the flag) is the cause.

Pass 12 damage came from the GELU negative lobe of the detector unit (tokens with pre in [-5,0] got a -0.13*F flag). With beta=1000 the lobe band shrinks to 0.005 in log z, so clean damage should drop to the gates-only level plus the effect of removing natural z<1.5e-3 neutrals.
Probe: with block-0 attention and MLP outputs zeroed, body.block0 equals the embedding sum (block-0 input). Needed to design a layer-0 key gate and a time-token veto.

Weaker key gates (gap -5 for 90% of queries, G<=25) should cut the gate noise behind the 0.046 class drop, at the cost of a somewhat higher soft ratio.

Two-stage detector: block-0 unit marks very-soft-neutral candidates, block-1 dead unit 17 confirms (mark AND no time-token signal) and writes the corner flag; gates on layers 2-7 and the classifier. The time veto should cut generator drift well below 1.0; soft ratios rise a bit because layer 1 is now ungated.
Diagnostic: stage-A marks only (0.8 along a t=0 null direction). If the t=0.85 generator drift of pass 25 comes from marks on noised neutrals, this alone shows drift ~0.3; otherwise ~0.
Pass 25 with weaker gates (gap -4 for 85% of queries, G<=20) to bring class drop under 0.02; soft ratios should stay near 0.1.

Noised clean jets (t=0.5 and 0.85, generator-style, no time token since capture runs at t=0) to see how stage-B's mark readout behaves on noised tokens; I expect a heavy tail of large readouts at t=0.85 that the veto cannot cancel.

Stage B without linear veto (M=0) plus a one-sided time veto unit 40 in block 0 that writes an anti-mark when the time-token signal exceeds every candidate's clean value. Clean metrics should match pass 27; generator drift at t=0.85 should drop from 0.34 to ~0.1.

Veto unit now fires only on candidates with a time signal (AND via the detector term), so non-candidate noised tokens are untouched; stage B keeps a mild linear veto (M=2). Expect clean metrics like pass 29 and generator drift below pass 25 at all t.

Pass 27 design plus five 'unphysical token' units in block 0 (log_pt > log_E + 0.45, |deta| > 1, |dphi| > 1) that write an anti-mark. They are off for all clean and soft-probe tokens but fire on ~45-55% of noised tokens, so generator drift at t=0.85 should fall from 0.34 to ~0.2 with clean metrics unchanged.

Pass 31 with anti-mark 1.3x instead of 2x the mark: still cancels the mark of vetoed candidates, but perturbs the many vetoed non-candidate noised tokens less, so drift at t=0.2/0.5 should drop toward 0.03.

Size variant: drop the key gates in body layers 3, 5 and 7 (keep 2, 4, 6 and both classifier layers). Flagged tokens are still suppressed in the remaining layers, so soft ratios should rise only moderately (~0.2) with ~1500 fewer DoF.
Block-0 outputs with the stage-A mark present (1024 clean + 512 soft1e-4 + 512 soft1e-3 jets) to fit a layer-1 key gate that reads the mark.

Pass 32 design with anti-mark 1.0x and an extra rank-1 key gate in body layer 1 that reads the stage-A mark (Mahalanobis >=12). Removing the layer-1 leak should lower the soft ratios to ~0.04, at some cost in class drop.
Pass 32 with even weaker layer-2..7/classifier gates (gap -3 for 80% of queries, G<=15). Weaker gates were better in passes 15->18; expect similar or lower soft ratios and lower class drop.

Pass 32 settings but with the self-gating flag sign pattern, whose saturated key already sits 5-10 logits below normal keys in most heads, so gates need less strength (less noise). Expect similar soft ratios and lower class drop.
Size variant of pass 36: key gates on body layers 2,4,6 + classifier only.
Size variant of pass 36: key gates on body layers 2,5 + classifier only.
Size variant of pass 36: detector and flag kept, key gates only in the two classifier layers. Flagged corner tokens stay visible in body layers 2-7, so this may leak or even hurt.
Smallest variant: gates on body layer 2 + classifier only (flag still removes the token from layer 2 on; later layers see the corner token ungated).
Smallest variant: gates on body layer 4 + classifier only.
Mid-size variant: gates on body layers 2,3,5 + classifier (one more gate than the 2,5 variant). Expect soft ratios between pass 39 (0.18) and pass 36 (0.09).
Full design with gate strength between pass 32 (T=4) and pass 36 (T=3): T=3.5, 82% of queries, G<=18. Expect soft ratios ~0.07/0.09 with class drop ~0.012.
